notes: CONCLUSIVE (irrebuttable) presumption under § 45-19.1-4 — any type of cancer in a firefighter is conclusively presumed occupational. For firefighters hired AFTER July 22, 2020: presumption does not apply if (1) pre-employment physical revealed cancer, (2) fewer than 2 years of employment, or (3) regular/habitual tobacco use in 5 years prior to diagnosis. Applies retroactively to cancer claims pending on or after July 22, 2020. Covers active firefighters (during service) and retired municipal firefighters (§ 45-19.1-3 — covers retired members retroactively).

Rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence. The law was enacted June 27, 2023 (P.L. 2023, ch. 360/361). It originally set a new-hire cutoff of July 1, 2023, but that cutoff was later moved to July 1, 2025 (P.L. 2025, ch. 440/441). For firefighters hired after July 1, 2025, the presumption does not apply if (1) a pre-employment physical exam already found heart disease or hypertension, or (2) the firefighter regularly used tobacco products during the 5 years before diagnosis. Firefighters hired before July 1, 2025 are not subject to either restriction.

condition_specific: smoke inhalation of the lungs or respiratory tract resulting in total disability or death
notes: Covers uniformed members of PAID fire departments only. City or town may adopt this presumption by ordinance — not automatically statewide. Presumption is rebuttable by competent evidence. Pre-employment (or subsequent) physical must not have revealed evidence of condition.

condition_specific: infectious disease including HIV (HBV, HCV) and other transmissible diseases
notes: Infectious disease defined as any condition transmissible by association with the sick or their secretions/excretions, excluding common cold; explicitly includes HIV, HBV, HCV. Disease must develop or manifest as a result of exposure during period while fire fighter or police officer is in service of department. Covers paid and volunteer fire departments. Entitles to occupational disability benefits under ch. 19 of title 45.

condition_specific: infectious disease including HIV (HBV, HCV) and other transmissible diseases
notes: Statute explicitly covers both fire fighters AND police officers. Disease must manifest during period of active service. Same definition of infectious disease as firefighter row.

condition_specific: post-traumatic stress disorder / post-traumatic stress injury (qualifying condition for accidental disability retirement)
filing_deadline_notes: 18-month filing deadline; subject to a three-physician confirmation process
notes: Entirely missing from the prior JSON, which only carried the later § 45-19-1(a)(2) IOD/salary-continuation PTSD track. This is a SECOND, separate PTSD track: PTSD was added as a qualifying condition for accidental disability retirement (66⅔% of final compensation) by P.L. 2021, ch. 391 and ch. 392, effective July 16, 2021 -- notably, PTSD was recognized on this PENSION track THREE YEARS BEFORE it was recognized on the IOD/salary-continuation track (2024, see the § 45-19-1(a)(2) row). Rhode Island should be coded as a non-WC, dual pension/IOD-benefit state (comparable to Indiana, Iowa, South Dakota), not a workers' compensation presumption state.

PTSD must be diagnosed by licensed mental health professional with a master's degree. Must arise from exposure to potentially traumatic events in course of employment or off-duty emergency assistance within Rhode Island. Presumption is rebuttable by fair preponderance of evidence that PTSI/PTSD is not job-related. PTSD arising from disciplinary action, work evaluation, job transfer, layoff, demotion, termination or adverse job action not covered.
